abstention_appropriateness.definition: Pass: answers an answerable question or clearly states insufficient supplied evidence for an unanswerable one without invention. Fail: invented answer or unwarranted abstention. Empty nonanswers fail.

answer_completeness.definition: Pass: answers the specific question completely. Fail: empty, evasive, missing requested fact or unwarranted abstention. Not applicable for insufficient-evidence cases.

attribution.definition: Pass: each answer claim has correctly attributed supporting document(s). Fail: missing citation or wrong/irrelevant document, even if its ID exists. Not applicable for appropriate insufficiency without factual answer claims.

human_assessability.definition: Assessable: raw content allows semantic judgment even with invalid JSON. Partial: only some content assessable. Unassessable: absent or uninterpretable text; leave semantic fields uncertain or null, not zero.

notes.definition: Explain each claim, support/contradictions, attribution, quotation relevance and endpoint decision. Flag ambiguous keys independently of deployment behavior.

quotation_relevance.definition: For a requested quote, pass only when exact text from its named source supports the requested answer in context. Missing requested quote fails. Judge volunteered quotes too; no quote requested or given is not applicable.

response_behavior.definition: Distinguish evidence insufficiency from refusal to perform the task and empty content; use raw text rather than parser status.

semantic_source_support.definition: Supported: every substantive factual claim follows from the supplied documents. Unsupported: claims invent or contradict facts; mixed: both supported and unsupported. Insufficient: appropriately explains missing evidence without invention. Inspect claim by claim; record reasons in notes.

task_success.definition: Answerable: complete requested factual answer, all substantive content source-supported, correctly attributed support, and any requested quotation accurate and relevant. Insufficient: explicitly acknowledge insufficient supplied evidence without inventing an answer. Judge raw text regardless of format. Uncertain if unable to decide; never infer success from valid IDs alone.
